key_insight: A semi-analytical geometric method synthesizes robust single-qubit controls in tens of milliseconds rather than minutes.
engineering_relevance: Faster pulse synthesis could reduce quantum-control design overhead while suppressing quasistatic amplitude and dephasing errors.
method: Map quantum evolution to space curves using Space Curve Quantum Control and the Frenet–Serret frame.
Apply the Pontryagin Maximum Principle and solve the resulting boundary-value problem by shooting.
Build a reference-solution library and interpolate initial guesses for new target rotations.
evidence_signal: Across 2,000 single-qubit rotations, mean local optimization took 39.945 ms per gate after interpolation-base preparation; simulated propagation gave nominal infidelities below 10^-9 after virtual phase correction and verified quasistatic-error robustness.
watch_item: The reported timing excludes interpolation-base preparation, and the abstract does not report hardware validation or robustness to time-varying noise.
paper_title: Semi-Analytical Geometric Synthesis of Robust Quantum Controls
